messages:
kai: Quick alert — p95 host-side latency +18% after the last small runtime change. Root cause looks like extra handshake/parse overhead on short requests.
ana: What metric surfaced it?
matt: Traced via ingress.latency.{p50,p95,p99} and host.parse_cpu. p95 jumped from 62ms -> 74ms for short (<=32 token) calls.
priyanka: Flame shows a lot of time in tokenization + parse path on host, not gpu. Host CPU spikes ~20% on smallest boxes.
lee: Any change to batching heuristics or kernel selection in that deploy?
kai: We pushed two things: (1) adaptive-batcher tweak to prefer throughput at 8s window, (2) kernel probe that falls back to scalar path for certain seq len checks.
nana: Could the batcher change increase micro-batches so we hit extra request framing overhead? especially over HTTP/2 + gRPC.
matt: Yes — more micro-batching means more small writev syscalls and more HPACK frames. Observed increase in smallwrites count per request.
priyanka: I captured a short trace from canary node:
```
INGRESS recv 0.9ms -> parse 5.2ms -> tokenize 7.8ms -> writev(1) 0.4ms -> grpc: frame serialize 2.1ms -> response send
```
Notable: tokenize+parse > 60% of host time for these requests.
lee: KV cache hit-rate also down 8% on that traffic window. Might be that micro-batches reduce prefix reuse.
kai: Good call. If batching changes alter request grouping, the KV cache (prefix/KVcache) loses locality and we pay tokenization/reprefix cost more.
nana: We should triage two vectors in parallel: revert adaptive-batcher tweak on canary + run synthetic short-request microbench with old/new batcher to compare KV-hit and syscall profile.
matt: I can run microbench now against canary 3.2 and 3.3 and dump perf counters + strace for smallwrites.
priyanka: I'll produce flamegraphs and a KV-access heatmap from the same runs.
devops-bot: Deploy 3.3 -> canary group initiated by matt at 1777777789.
lee: Also check kernel selection logs — the scalar fallback probe logs a reason code when it switches; add a debug sample when seq_len<48.
kai: Action items: matt -> bench + strace, priyanka -> flame + kv-heatmap, lee -> enable kernel-probe debug on canary. If p95 still high after revert, we look at HTTP2 framing path.
nana: If we confirm KV locality is the cause, workaround: prefer stable batch grouping by trace-id or small adaptive threshold for short requests.
matt: Running bench, ETA 10m. Will paste artifacts.
priyanka: Thx — tagging infra on-call if we need immediate rollback: @oncall-infra.
lee: Also note: this regression mainly shows up for hosted API tier with many single-turn prompts. Dedicated customers less affected.
kai: Good to know. Post results here and we'll decide rollback vs targeted fix. :thumbsup:
